## Per-case notes

### eval-form-input-invalid-amount-fields — 88/100 (pass)
All three critical criteria are met: each of the five invalid fields shows its own specific Ukrainian message, and none of them is in the error-free list. The content criteria (4–7) are fully met, because each message gives the rule and a concrete example, and both day-count messages name which term they refer to. Points come off only for the wording 'Невірний' (a calque) in the unit-price message, which also opens by stating the error rather than what to enter, and for the missing full stop at the end of each message.

### eval-form-input-invalid-customer-fields — 85/100 (pass)
Both critical criteria are met. Every invalid field, including the address made of only spaces, shows its own specific message in Ukrainian, and none of those fields appears in the list of fields without errors. The email, phone, name, address and service messages each meet their own criterion, with examples where the rubric asks for them. Points were taken off for criterion 8: the email and phone messages are two sentences each, and the way examples are introduced and punctuated is not consistent across fields.

### eval-form-input-missing-iban-render-error — 79/100 (pass)
Both critical criteria are met. The alert is visible and states \"Немає IBAN для валюти EUR\", which names the cause and the currency. It also gives the fix location, Settings → supplier profile, with a link, and does not blame the user's form. Points are deducted because the location is repeated at the end as a separate link fragment (\"Налаштуваннях → профіль постачальника. Налаштування → профіль постачальника\"). This makes the text redundant and clumsy, and I would not ship it as-is. | Both critical criteria are met: the alert renders and says 'Немає IBAN для валюти EUR.' It also says where to fix the problem ('Налаштуваннях → профіль постачальника') without blaming the user. The main flaw is a copy problem: the link text repeats the location as a fragment after the sentences. A user sees 'профіль постачальника. Налаштування → профіль постачальника', which looks unfinished, so it would need a fix before shipping. That costs criterion 4 partial credit and keeps the score below 90.

### eval-new-invoice-empty-no-supplier — 70/100 (FAIL)
Both critical criteria are met: the empty state names the missing supplier profile, links to Settings, and the preview shows guidance. The export buttons are also disabled. Points come off for three things. Two places say that filling the form updates the preview, which conflicts with the real blocker (the missing profile). The paste helper uses English ('key: value' and English example keys), which breaks the Ukrainian-only rule. That same helper is also too technical for a non-technical user. Total deductions put the score just below the pass threshold. | Both critical criteria are met: the page has a clear banner explaining the supplier-profile requirement with a link to Settings, and the preview shows guidance instead of a blank frame. Export buttons are disabled, so criterion 3 is met. Points are deducted because the subtitle and preview header tell users to fill in the form without linking that to the profile blocker. The paste helper also uses English and technical wording (\"key: value\", English keys in the example) that a non-technical user may not understand. The page works but has copy-coherence issues I would fix before shipping.

### eval-client-directory-empty-state — 82/100 (pass)
Both critical criteria are met. The empty state says \"Поки немає жодного клієнта\" and offers \"Додати клієнта\" as the action. The page explains the benefit (filling in invoice data) and the storage location (\"зберігається в браузері\"), and all copy is in Ukrainian. I took points off because the search field is still shown on the empty directory with nothing showing it is disabled, and because the benefit message and the add button each appear twice.

### eval-client-directory-validation-errors — 79/100 (pass)
Both critical criteria are met. All three messages are in Ukrainian, name the missing field, and tell the user what to do with 'Вкажіть …'. The name and address messages are identical to the invoice form's wording. The email message adds an example ('Приклад: billing@client.example') that the invoice form's 'Вкажіть email' does not have. That breaks consistency with the invoice form, the one-sentence rule and uniform punctuation, so points come off criteria 4 and 5. | Both critical criteria are met. Every message names its field ('ім'я або назву клієнта', 'адресу клієнта', 'email'), all are in Ukrainian, and each gives an imperative 'Вкажіть …' instruction. The name and address messages match the invoice form's wording exactly. The email message differs: it adds a 'Приклад:' sentence that the invoice form's plain 'Вкажіть email' does not have. That extra sentence also breaks the one-sentence, consistent-punctuation rule, so criteria 4 and 5 are only partly met.

### eval-invoice-registry-empty-state — 94/100 (pass)
Both critical criteria pass. The page has an explicit empty-state line ('Поки немає жодного рахунку.') and a clear first-invoice button ('Створити перший рахунок'). The status badges are labelled 'Можливі статуси:', so they read as a legend and not as data. The page explains what the list will show, says the data stays in the browser without technical jargon, and is entirely in Ukrainian. Points come off for the two create buttons ('Новий рахунок' and 'Створити перший рахунок') shown together on an empty page, which slightly weakens which one is the main action. Points also come off because the badge legend appears as an unseparated run of words in the rendered text, so a quick reader may not see it as a legend.

### eval-ui-copy-validation-messages-uk — 58/100 (FAIL)
The gating criterion is met because every message is in Ukrainian. Criterion 5 fails because invoice-form and client-dialog messages have no final period while supplier-profile and preview messages do, and 'Вкажіть email' gets an example in one place but not the other. Criterion 7 fails because empty IBAN fields show 'Некоректний IBAN' with no guidance or example, and the date error gives only a pattern. Calques like 'більше нуля' and 'Невірний' make criterion 2 only partly met, which brings the score below the 70 pass threshold. | The output fails with a score of 57 because two non-critical criteria are fully missed and two more are only partly met. The one critical criterion (all messages in Ukrainian) is met, and there are no lowercase starts or blaming phrases. Punctuation is clearly inconsistent across surfaces: supplier-profile messages end with periods, while invoice-form and client-dialog messages do not. BC-UX-01 is not fully met: the date and IBAN messages lack examples, and an empty IBAN field gets an 'incorrect' message instead of telling the user what to enter. Minor grammar and wording issues ('більше нуля', 'Невірний') and the mixed use of 'Невірний' and 'Некоректний' lower the score further.

### eval-document-render-eur-full-prepayment — 76/100 (pass)
All four critical criteria are met. The amounts are correct in EUR with no USD. With 100% prepayment, the remaining balance is shown as '0.00'. There are no template artefacts, and every bilingual label from the fixed template appears in both English and Ukrainian (I checked docs/invoice-template.html). Points come off for two things: the service description is a 360° virtual-tour point, not the '3D visualization of an interior' that was requested, and the amounts in the total and payment-terms rows have no currency next to them. | All four critical criteria pass. The amounts are correct in EUR, the 100% prepayment leaves a remaining balance of 0.00, there are no template artefacts, and every label the template renders in both languages appears in both. The English-only labels match docs/invoice-template.html. There are two deductions. First, the service text describes a 360° virtual-tour point instead of the entered '3D visualization of an interior'. Second, no amount has the currency written next to it, which matters most in the payment-terms row because it has no column header. The result is a solid but imperfect document, a little above the pass line.
